report.headline: Usage projected to climb from 20.9% to 25.1% in the EuroLeague, but the shooting-efficiency projection carries no signal

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 25.1% in the EuroLeague, up from 20.9% in the 2020-21 NBA season, moving the subject from just above the NBA average (+0.15 sd) to above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted mean of 20.2% (sd 4.7%).

risks.text: Source-season true shooting was 49.0%, 1.46 standard deviations below the NBA average that year, and the fitted NBA->EL carry-over slope on efficiency alone is only 0.534, meaning most of that shortfall would not simply wash out with the league change.

The true shooting projection of 54.0% cannot be relied on: the model's error (4.7%) ties the trivial baseline (4.7%) on this metric, so it adds no information beyond guessing the EuroLeague average of 57.4%.

Players who actually make the NBA->EL move have historically sat 0.31 standard deviations below their own league's average, while this subject sat 0.15 standard deviations above it, making the fitted cohort a somewhat atypical comparison for this specific case.

Even on usage, the 95% interval spans 17.8% to 32.3%, roughly three standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution, so any single-season usage figure could land far from the 25.1% point estimate.

strengths.text: Produced 15.311 points per 75 possessions on a modest 20.9% NBA usage rate, with an 8.6% assist rate and 4.352 rebounds per 75 possessions.
Turned the ball over at only a 5.4% rate in the source season, suggesting secure ball-handling to build an expanded role around.

The usage-rate model beats the trivial league-mean baseline (3.3% mean absolute error versus 4.3%) across 115 historical NBA->EL transitions, so the projected rise to 25.1% usage is a genuine signal rather than noise.

uncertainty.text: The 80% interval for usage runs 20.3%-29.8% and the 95% interval 17.8%-32.3%, a span exceeding two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution, so the model can rank this player among movers but cannot pin down an individual figure; the true shooting projection of 54.0% (80% interval 46.1%-62.0%) should not be trusted at all, since its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the EuroLeague league-mean baseline (4.7%).
